text: detection probability varies across sectors due survey effort, visibility, habitat, mean group size (mean_group_size, computed automatically inside doas()), can pass one-sided R formula p_formula. can also model sector-level abundance function habitat covariates via n_formula generate predictions predict(): ML (method = "ML", default): Fits quasi-binomial logistic regression (p_hat ~ covariates, weighted G_est) sectors (p_formula) /quasi-Poisson log-link regression detection-adjusted abundance (n_formula). Competing models can compared using QAIC(). (Also accepts method = "frequentist"). Bayes (method = "Bayes"): Runs multi-chain Metropolis-within-Gibbs regression coupled posterior draws latent group abundance GiG_i, reporting posterior means, standard deviations, 95% credible intervals, R̂\hat{R}, ESS every regression coefficient. what: Accounting for Sampling Effort, Transect Length, and Area Offsets (offset())
title: DOAS Tutorial: Analyzing Real Survey Data and Running Simulations
text: field surveys transects management sectors unequal size (e.g. transects different lengths sectors different surface areas), longer transects larger sectors naturally intercept animals simply area sampled. DOAS, can model directly including offset() n_formula: log⁡(λj)=log⁡(effortj)+β0+β1⋅habitatj\log(\lambda_j) = \log(\text{effort}_j) + \beta_0 + \beta_1 \cdot \text{habitat}_j offset() fixes coefficient exactly 1.01.0 log scale, meaning expected abundance scales proportionally sampling effort, remaining regression coefficients represent density per unit effort area. Note Detection vs. Abundance: - transect length sector size alters number animals present sampled unit, put offset(log(transect_length)) n_formula. - transect length survey duration alters well observers spot animals (e.g. observer fatigue long walks search speed), include unconstrained covariate p_formula = ~ fatigue. - offset() fully supported frequentist Bayesian models (well predict.doas()!).

code: library(DOAS)  # 1. Simulate a 24-sector population (~3500 animals) with a habitat effect on abundance, #    and a partial DOAS survey (12 DO sectors, 12 Block sectors) with an effort effect on detection set.seed(12) pop <- simulate_pop(   pop_size   = 3500,   mean_group = 8,   tot_areas  = 24,   n_formula  = ~ habitat,   n_betas    = c(habitat = 0.5) ) raw_data <- simulate_survey(   sim_pop         = pop,   det_p1          = 0.55,   intra_group_det = 1.0,   det_group       = 0.95,   obs_effect      = 0.90,   detvar          = 0.02,   surv_areas      = 12,   p_formula       = ~ effort,   p_betas         = c(effort = 1.0) )  survey_dat <- doas_data(raw_data, format = "sector") print(head(survey_dat))  # 2. Maximum Likelihood (ML) Estimation (Detection & Abundance Covariates) fit_ml_cov <- doas(   survey_dat,   method    = "ML",   obs_type  = "independent",   pooling   = "hybrid",   p_formula = ~ effort,   n_formula = ~ habitat )  fit_ml_null <- doas(   survey_dat,   method    = "ML",   obs_type  = "independent",   pooling   = "hybrid",   p_formula = ~ 1,   n_formula = ~ habitat )  summary(fit_ml_cov) cat("True simulated population:", pop$tot_pop, "\n") QAIC(fit_ml_cov, fit_ml_null)  # Predict detection probability and expected abundance across a covariate gradient new_sectors <- data.frame(effort = c(-1, 0, 1), habitat = c(-1, 0, 1)) predict(fit_ml_cov, newdata = new_sectors, type = "detection") predict(fit_ml_cov, newdata = new_sectors, type = "abundance")  # 3. Multi-Chain Hierarchical Bayesian Estimation & WAIC Selection fit_bayes_null <- doas(   survey_dat,   method   = "Bayes",   obs_type = "independent",   pooling  = "hybrid",   chains   = 3,   iter     = 2000,   burnin   = 500 )  fit_bayes_cov <- doas(   survey_dat,   method    = "Bayes",   obs_type  = "independent",   pooling   = "hybrid",   p_formula = ~ effort,   n_formula = ~ habitat,   chains    = 3,   iter      = 2000,   burnin    = 500 )  summary(fit_bayes_cov) WAIC(fit_bayes_null, fit_bayes_cov)
